reference.title: Dumbbell Drag Biceps Curl
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Upper Arms, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you curl up, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2.4 s down

prescription.progression: Load is user-chosen: pick a dumbbell you can curl for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion); add reps, then weight. Use less weight than for a standard curl; the dumbbells must stay in contact with the body (clinical opinion).

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width, dumbbells in front of the thighs, palms forward, handles touching the legs.
Breathe out and drag the dumbbells straight up the front of the body: the elbows travel back, not forward.
Squeeze at the lower chest, elbows behind the trunk, shoulders down and back.
Breathe in and slide the dumbbells back down the body to straight arms.
Arms straight, handles at the thighs, repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the elbows swing forward (it turns into a normal curl)
mistakes.fix: Think "elbows back": the dumbbells stay against the body all the way up.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging or rolling the shoulders forward at the top
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest up and the shoulders down and back.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to start the weight
mistakes.fix: Brace the trunk; lighten the dumbbells.

mistakes.mistake: Dumbbells drifting away from the body
mistakes.fix: Keep the handles brushing the thighs and abdomen.

kinematics.norm: Full range: mean elbow range was about 117-123 degrees across barbell, EZ-bar and alternating dumbbell curls (Marcolin 2018)

kinematics.measure: Forearm rotation (wrist pron channel, 0 = palm up/forward, 90 = thumb up)
kinematics.norm: The supinated grip gave the highest biceps activity in the lifting phase; neutral grips shift work toward the brachioradialis (Coratella 2023)

kinematics.measure: Upper arm from the trunk line (sagittal)
kinematics.norm: The upper arm moves back behind the trunk line (shoulder extension) as the dumbbells rise, the defining feature of the drag curl (clinical opinion); shoulder-extended curls load the biceps long head at long lengths (Attarieh 2025)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2-3 s down (clinical opinion); biceps activity was lower while lowering than lifting at the same load (Oliveira 2009)
Vertical path close to the body with the elbows travelling back (clinical opinion; no kinematic study of the drag curl was found)

sources.title: GymVisual #368712, Dumbbell Drag Biceps Curl, video (movement reference)

cautions: Elbow or shoulder pain: lighten the dumbbell and shorten the range; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Keep the wrists straight (in line with the forearm); a bent-back wrist under load strains the forearm (clinical opinion).
Pick the dumbbells up and set them down with a straight back and bent knees.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Front-of-shoulder discomfort as the elbows go back: shorten the pull and keep the shoulders down (clinical opinion).
modify: Shoulder discomfort: reduce how far the elbows travel back.

muscleNotes.biceps_r: Main elbow flexor; the elbows travel back so the shoulder ends in extension, the same shoulder-extended position as the incline and Bayesian curls. Extended-shoulder and flexed-shoulder curls built the biceps similarly over 10 weeks (Attarieh 2025).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Main elbow flexor; the elbows travel back so the shoulder ends in extension, the same shoulder-extended position as the incline and Bayesian curls. Extended-shoulder and flexed-shoulder curls built the biceps similarly over 10 weeks (Attarieh 2025).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Brachioradialis (mapped to the forearm extensor region) assists elbow flexion, most with the forearm near neutral.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Wrist and finger flexors hold the handle and keep the wrist straight.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulder so the upper arm stays put; it rises if the elbow drifts forward.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulder so the upper arm stays put; it rises if the elbow drifts forward.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still so the hips do not swing the weight up.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Draws the elbows back behind the trunk as the dumbbells rise.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Draws the elbows back behind the trunk as the dumbbells rise.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Hold the shoulder blades back so the shoulders do not roll forward as the elbows go back.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Hold the shoulder blades back so the shoulders do not roll forward as the elbows go back.
